summary: Angels Camp sits at roughly 1,400 feet in the western Sierra Nevada foothills of Calaveras County, and its most famous claim — hosting the annual Jumping Frog Jubilee inspired by Mark Twain's 1865 short story — is not a quaint exaggeration but a real, sanctioned competition that has drawn crowds since 1928. That literary oddity hints at the town's texture: a 3.6-square-mile Gold Rush–era settlement where Main Street still runs through historic stone-and-brick buildings, and the surrounding terrain rolls with oak-studded hills and seasonal grasslands rather than suburban cul-de-sacs. At a median household income of roughly $60,400 against a median home value near $444,400, the price-to-income ratio lands around 7.4× — steep for a rural foothill town, though monthly rents averaging $1,732 reflect limited housing stock more than urban demand. With annual daytime highs averaging 71°F and nearly 9.5 hours of sunshine daily, summers run hot and dry while winters stay mild by Sierra standards. There is no major employer hub here; the economy leans on services, tourism, and county government, making this largely a place where many commute outward or work remotely. Angels Camp is a town whose identity was literally written into American literature before it had paved roads — and that past still outweighs its present economic gravity.
